line: Bleedin’ concrete, bet you niggas won’t come ’cross the street
vault_lines: Bleedin' concrete, bet you niggas won't come 'cross the street
meaning:
After living a hard life on his neighborhood, Kodak considers that he has the streets in his blood, thus, he’s “bleeding concrete.”

Kodak warns to his competition that they wouldn’t want to face him, he represents the streets he came from and they would regret it sooner than later.

line: On my Ps and Qs, on them jiggas, call me jiggaboo
vault_lines: On my Ps and Qs, on them jiggas, call me jiggaboo
meaning:
‘Ps and Qs’ is a reference to the English expression “Mind your Ps and Qs” which essentially means “be on your best behavior.” ‘Ps & Qs’ can also be a drug reference in relation to amount he consumes: Pounds & Quarter pounds

‘Jigga’ is slang for ecstasy in Louisiana—Baton Rouge-based rapper Lil Boosie popularized the term.

‘Jiggaboo’ is a slang term for a dark skinned person of African descent.

line: Project baby, y’all was skippin’ in the hallway, I was skippin’ schoo
vault_lines: Project baby, y'all was skippin' in the hallway, I was skippin' school
meaning:
Kodak grew up in the ghetto in Florida. His childhood nickname soon became the “Project Baby,” since he was born in the projects—a building complex used to house tens to hundreds of broke families. Kodak titled his first album, Project Baby, after this nickname.

Kodak Black told Pigeons and Planes about his time as a student:


I would leave class and all that. I was being kicked out of lots of schools and had to go to alternative schools. Just because I was missing so many days of school for being locked up, and I’d have to come back out and try to learn myself. But you know, I’d always try to do it.

I ain’t graduate just ‘cause of that little incident I was in. I was on my way to graduation. I was in the 12th grade, I was gonna graduate, I paid for my grad badge, I was on my way to prom and all that. And I just got caught up in January and they detained me. When I was detained, I earned my GED in there.

line: Don’t you ask me where the pole at, where yo clothes at? I ain’t talkin’ ’bout my niggas, dammit, but y’all trippin’, too Is it you? Damn, my nigga, what the hell got into you?
vault_lines: Don't you ask me where the pole at, where yo clothes at?
meaning: Here, Kodak realizes that even his closest friends have been using Flakka (Flocka), a synthetic drug similar to bath salts. Throughout the track, Kodak talks about users of Flakka, referring to “jackass” addicts whom he has no relation.

line: Smokin’ flocka, you a jackass, all I smoke is gas
vault_lines: Smokin' flocka, you a jackass, all I smoke is gas
meaning: “Flakka” is a designer drug popular in South Florida, also known as “gravel,” that can cause intense hallucinations. Kodak’s not into that—he only smokes high grade marijuana, otherwise known as “gas”.

line: I just bought a new old Jag, yeah, it’s so fast
vault_lines: I just bought a new old Jag, yeah, it's so fast
meaning: Instead of going for the newest model on the market, Kodak cops a vintage Jaguar. Maybe he bought the 60s Jaguar E-Type, which has a top speed of 149.8 mph and received praise from Ferrari founder Enzo Ferrari, who called it “the most beautiful car in the world.”

line: Pop a nigga like a damn tag, shoppin’ on they ass
vault_lines: Pop a nigga like a damn tag, shoppin' on they ass
meaning:
Kodak treats killing people like he’s perusing a storefront. He equates tags on clothes to toe-tags in the morgue.

“Pop” refers to both the sound a gun makes when fired and “poppin' tags”—a phrase used to describe removing the tags from new clothes.

line: I got old cash, spazzin’ on they ass I got Prada on my ho ass, got my last one mad
vault_lines: I got Prada on my ho ass, got my last one mad
meaning:
“Old money” is money that’s been sitting in one’s bank account for a while; that individual has so much money that a portion remains untouched for its lifetime. Although Kodak hasn’t inherited any wealth, he’s making so much “new money” that it feels like he has had it all along.

Prada is an Italian luxury fashion house. Now that Kodak has the wealth to buy his girl high-quality clothes, his ex is jealous since that could’ve been her.
